problem: '-cant' is not an English suffix; applicant is applic- (from apply) + the person suffix -ant, as in accountant (261), so '-cant(人)' teaches a fake suffix.

fix.m: apply 申請＋人 → 申請人

problem: The note says 'ci' before a vowel is read /ʃ/, but here the i is still pronounced (/priʃi/, ci is its own syllable); the -cial/-cious rule where i disappears does not apply.

fix.n: c 在 i＋母音前唸 /ʃ/，i 仍唸 /i/；-tion 前的 a 重讀唸 /eɪ/

problem: '-it' is the Latin past-participle ending, not an English noun suffix (submit, admit, commit are verbs; credit itself is also a verb), so '-it(名詞)' teaches a false Part 5 rule.

'un(一)' clashes with the negative prefix un- the learner just saw in unemployment (308), and '-ique' is not an English adjective suffix (technique, boutique are nouns), so the split confuses more than it helps.
'-estic' is a Latin ending (-esticus) presented as an English suffix; no such suffix exists, so the split is forced.
